items.candidate: Static verifier classification quality is not a sufficient optimization-safety proxy.
items.mechanism: Select and validate verifiers by downstream optimized-policy behavior under matched conditions, not fixed-set precision/recall alone.
items.uncertainty: Verifier/policy-family and optimization-distribution specific; the same study contains beneficial hybrid verifiers, so this is not evidence that model verifiers are generally worse than rules.
items.tested_scope: Qwen2.5-7B mathematical RL with rule/model/hybrid verifiers and tested DeepscaleR, Skywork-OR1, and WebInstruct-Verified→GPQA-Diamond settings.
items.quantitative_result: Static recall 0.49→0.62 and precision 0.68→0.73, yet Skywork-OR1 downstream 58.7→55.5; GPQA-Diamond base 36.4, general-verifier 45.0, R1-Distill-Verifier 35.9; one training reward diverged from a GPT-4o oracle after ~450 iterations.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: No O RL optimization loop uses a learned verifier as reward; this dynamic verifier-distribution-shift failure has not been tested.

items.candidate: Dense step correctness and earliest critical-error localization should be measured separately and combined with outcome evidence for selection.
items.mechanism: Use neutral/exploratory step labels, first-critical-error localization, and a process+outcome selector rather than outcome-only or step-accuracy-only evaluation.
items.uncertainty: Error-propagation labeling is evaluator-dependent; removing it improves some evaluators and hurts others, so label semantics require direct ablation.
items.tested_scope: 1,000 tool-agent trajectories / 8,509 labeled steps across HotPotQA, GAIA, BFCL and tau2-Bench; GAIA Best-of-8 selection.
items.quantitative_result: 89.1% IAA; strongest 81.6% StepAcc vs 65.8% FirstErrAcc; longest-quartile FirstErrAcc drops 10.79–21.67pp. Outcome→process Best-of-8 improved every listed generator, including 35.9→50.9 (+15.0pp).
items.why_new_relative_to_O: O records action traces and has related process-evaluation machinery, but no earliest-error metric, neutral label, or process+outcome selector is implemented.

items.candidate: Meta-evaluate research-agent judges with human-validated localized corruption pairs and mixed local/holistic judging.
items.mechanism: Inject controlled reasoning/tool/outcome defects with known ground truth, measure judge detection by category, and combine fine-grained local checks with holistic checks where global context matters.
items.uncertainty: Controlled localized perturbations do not exhaust natural interactive failures; some global-context failures favor holistic judging.
items.quantitative_result: 140 reasoning +132 tool-use +200 outcome perturbations; human κ=0.86. Best pointwise overall accuracy only 45.7% reasoning /54.5% tool /47.5% report; fine-grained vs holistic gains range +2.8 to +34.3pp in reported cells.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: O fail-closes evaluator provenance and scores behavior, but no controlled corruption-pair meta-evaluation of an LLM judge was found.

items.candidate: Allocate stochastic evaluation replications by decision-critical uncertainty/noise rather than equally.
items.mechanism: Use OCBA/ranking-and-selection style adaptive replication, guarded by finite-budget racing/elimination and an equal-allocation fallback when estimates are weak.
items.uncertainty: The 23x figure is a scoped classical simulation result; finite-budget OCBA can underperform equal allocation and O-like evaluation transfer is untested.
items.tested_scope: Reduced 210-design stochastic supply-chain resource-allocation simulation, probability-of-correct-selection target 99%.
items.quantitative_result: P(correct selection)=99% required budget 14,600 with OCBA versus 330,000 with equal allocation, reported up to 23x / ~96% simulation-time reduction in that setting.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: Current O has no OCBA/ranking-and-selection budget allocator or noise/gap-based replication schedule.

items.candidate: Route tasks to multi-agent topology by measured task structure instead of assuming multi-agent scaling helps.
items.mechanism: Condition Independent/Centralized/Decentralized/Hybrid topology on decomposability, sequentiality, tool intensity and baseline capability under matched controls.
items.uncertainty: Transfer outside the tested model/task/topology cells is open; topology controller overhead must be included.
items.tested_scope: 260 configurations, six benchmarks, five architectures, three LLM families.
items.quantitative_result: Relative performance vs single-agent ranged from +80.8% on a decomposable task to -70.0% on sequential planning; learned framework identified the best-performing architecture for 87% of held-out configurations.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: No MAS topology selector or topology-task matching evaluation was found in O.

items.candidate: Optional memory should be selectively injected with an explicit silence/no-op action rather than always exposed.
items.mechanism: A separate memory controller maintains structured state and chooses targeted reminders or silence based on expected action-time value.
items.uncertainty: Effect size is model/task dependent and helper quality matters; a weak memory model can hurt. Mandatory authority/control context is outside this learned gate.
items.tested_scope: Terminal-Bench 2.0 and tau2-Bench proactive-memory settings with Sonnet/Opus action models and memory-agent ablations.
items.quantitative_result: Sonnet Terminal-Bench 37.6→45.9 (+8.3pp); tau2 weighted 55.0→61.8 (+6.8pp). In tau2 Sonnet, selective memory 64.3/61.2 macro/micro vs full-bank-always-exposed 61.5/58.6; untrained helper degraded validation.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: O supports optional context but has no separate proactive reminder/no-op agent or matched proactive-memory benchmark result.

items.candidate: Evaluate agents under matched realistic network/server faults; generic recovery prompting is not uniformly sufficient.
items.mechanism: Inject controlled transport/server faults into otherwise matched agent runs and score final recovery outcome, not merely retry behavior.
items.uncertainty: Fault distributions, agents and benchmark scaffolds are specific; production retry/idempotency behavior can differ materially.
items.tested_scope: WAREX matched no-fault/network/server perturbations on WebArena, REAL and WebVoyager.
items.quantitative_result: WebArena 0.124 no-fault→0.037 network (-70%) /0.053 server (-57%); REAL 0.170→0.045 (-73%) /0.071 server (-58%); WebVoyager 0.420→0.020 (-95%) /0.300 (-28%). Recovery prompts only partially restore several cells.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: O has provider/block recovery policy, but no controlled web-agent network/server-fault robustness benchmark or comparable final-success measurement.

items.candidate: Autonomous meta-agent self-improvement evidence should include repeated-run variance, held-out verification and integrity/red-team checks.
items.mechanism: Treat improvement as a stochastic, adversarially auditable process; reject best-run-only evidence and require repeated runs plus resource/policy integrity.
items.uncertainty: MAC is a bounded proxy for recursive self-improvement, and repeated-run requirements must be cost-normalized.
items.tested_scope: Meta-Agent Challenge autonomous meta-agent configurations and zero-resource red-team proxy setting.
items.quantitative_result: Only 5/39 configurations exceeded corresponding human-baseline average; 33% had run-to-run std >0.1; zero-resource red-team produced clear policy violations in 7/8 trials and only 1 valid artifact.
items.why_new_relative_to_O: O has conservative candidate/regression boundaries but no MAC-style autonomous meta-agent benchmark, run-variance analysis or zero-resource red-team study.
